plan.description: Measure nonvoter contribution counting through actual verification registration, notification, tallying, and leaderLoop completion. Include a separate voter-supported control.

harness.description: Exclusive fixture ownership controls registration and one synchronous notifyAll call before leaderLoop starts. No replication workers run, so other contributions cannot occur. A distinct synthetic terminal future queued afterward on the same buffered verifyCh provides a FIFO processing endpoint. Its completion is followed by shutdown and a goroutine join before inspecting the primary future. The marker never enters a replication notification map. Separate fixtures exercise N and V1 contributions.
semantic_changes: Manually initialize fixed membership and one leader generation using actual Raft fields and setupLeaderState; omit election, persistent startup, no-op dispatch, transport, and replication workers.
Instantiate followerReplication objects using the fields and membership inclusion shown in startStopReplication; do not execute its asynchronous worker startup.
Call Raft.verifyLeader under exclusive ownership before starting leaderLoop instead of dispatching through public VerifyLeader.
Inject one affirmative notification through the selected actual followerReplication.notifyAll boundary.
Queue a separate initialized terminal future as a processing marker. Its manufactured tally controls stopping only and is never evidence of primary verification support.
Use a one-hour lease timeout to keep the lease outside the short experiment. Timeout or changed leader state prevents result emission.
Read primary completion from its actual error channel after joining leaderLoop; pending means no success by this controlled endpoint, not eventual noncompletion.

legality.derivation: The selected scope explicitly admits an affirmative nonvoter boundary input. Source shows remote nonvoters belong in the replication map, registration uses these objects, and notifyAll forwards contributions to vote. newCommitment initializes without notifying commitCh and gives startIndex 1 in this empty-log fixture; no commit processing is activated. Actual leaderLoop processes terminal verification notifications and responds to their futures. The separately queued marker establishes a processing endpoint without adding support to the primary. This is an isolated boundary execution, not a distributed reachability demonstration.
legality.applicability: Fixed mixed membership, one leader generation, serialized registration and delivery, and no other contributing workers. The measured endpoint is internal verification completion.
unresolved: The fixture does not establish a legal distributed history producing the affirmative response.
Manual replication-object construction is an adaptation supported by the observed producer, not an execution of that producer's worker startup.
The processing marker is a synthetic control operation, not a valid client verification or evidence of authority.

grounding.derivation: VerifyLeader promises leadership verification, AddNonvoter excludes election participation, and the verification consumer describes quorum agreement while deriving its threshold from voters. Together these support the accepted eligibility inference. The oracle independently counts configured voter identities among the local contributor and the delivered remote contributor. The observed success field comes only from the primary future's actual completion channel after actual leaderLoop processing.
grounding.applicability: For the nonvoter case, successful completion with insufficient configured voter support violates the selected obligation. The separate voter case checks a representative permitted completion path.
unresolved: Voter eligibility is an attributed inference from combined responsibilities; the public API does not explicitly prescribe the verification algorithm.
The result does not establish public-call behavior in a distributed execution or stale reads.
alternatives: A sourced mechanism establishing voter-backed authority independently could require reassessing the eligibility interpretation.

observable_properties.description: Compare actual internal verification success at the completed processing endpoint with independently derived voter support. Local L plus nonvoter N must not complete successfully; local L plus voter V1 supplies the representative permitted quorum. Failure of the permitted control alone does not establish nonvoter substitution.

uncertainties: Distributed response reachability, request freshness, membership changes, generation transitions, transport correlation, and stale-read consequences remain unresolved.
The primary can remain pending at the completed boundary endpoint; this establishes only absence of success through that endpoint.
Marker failure, timeout, missing registration, changed leader state, or failed goroutine join produces no property result.
Internal completion is measured directly; public VerifyLeader dispatch and client observation are not exercised.

partial_design: Retains O_verify_voter_support and all five selected bindings. The attached commitment implementation resolves the initialization dependency. The complete harness replaces the unsafe cross-channel rendezvous with a separate terminal processing marker on verifyCh; it cannot contribute to the primary. Registration, admitted contribution, controlled endpoint completion, and independent result are correlated by operation_id.
